# Ingot

Ingot is a Bittensor subnet. A fixed open-source teacher model in BF16 is the reference.
Miners submit quantized copies of it with the same architecture, no larger than genesis. The validator measures how
far each copy drifts from the teacher, token by token and layer by layer, and crowns the copy
that beats the current king by a margin. Every king is mirrored to Hugging Face under
https://huggingface.co/dendriteholdings as `Ingot-<roman numeral>-27B-FP8`. The newest five
kings share the emission for five days each; the rest burns to uid 0.

The model to beat is always the newest king. Before the first coronation it is genesis.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Teacher | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16) |
| Genesis | `dendriteholdings/Ingot-genesis-27B-FP8` |
| Source of truth | `chain.toml` in this repo |

## What a submission must be

- The genesis model: `config.json` equals genesis on every value except the free keys
  (`quantization_config.weight_block_size`, `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert`,
  `transformers_version`, `use_cache`, `initializer_range`, `attention_dropout`), and holds no
  key genesis does not. `quant_method` is `fp8`.
- The genesis tensors: every weight of `dendriteholdings/Ingot-genesis-27B-FP8` keeps its name and shape, nothing
  is added; scale tensors are not compared to genesis, they follow your block size. In the text model a weight may be BF16 or F32, or FP8 E4M3 where genesis has it in FP8:
  vLLM serves nothing else quantized (an FP8 `embed_tokens` does not load). The projections vLLM
  fuses into one layer (`q/k/v_proj`, `gate/up_proj`, `in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z`,
  `in_proj_b/in_proj_a`) are all FP8 or all unquantized. Tensors
  under `model.visual.`, `mtp.` and `lm_head.` keep the genesis dtype (`lm_head` stays BF16: the
  evaluator applies it itself to your last hidden state). An FP8 weight `x.weight` carries
  `x.weight_scale_inv` shaped by your `weight_block_size` (two ints, 128 or larger), and
  `modules_to_not_convert` lists exactly the text linears you left unquantized. Every value is
  finite: a NaN or an infinity anywhere rejects the model. Weight values
  are yours: quantize, fine-tune, distill, as you like.
- No larger than genesis: all `*.safetensors` together at most 30,866,866,928 bytes.
- Exactly these files, all at the top level: `config.json`, `model.safetensors.index.json`
  and the `*.safetensors` shards the index names (names are free). Any other file, including
  the tokenizer, README or LICENSE, rejects the submission; the validator uses the genesis
  copies, and a king is published with them added.

`ingot check-model --path ./my-model` runs these checks locally. A rejected submission shows
its reason in the status the validator publishes (below).

## Your own quantization, not someone else's

Before the evaluation the validator fingerprints your weights: what is left of them once every
rearrangement that leaves the model's output unchanged is undone (permuted or rescaled
neurons, heads and channels, moved norm gains, a permuted, rotated or rescaled residual stream)
is your quantization error against the teacher. Independent quantizations make unrelated
errors. The fingerprint is compared with genesis and with every earlier submission of other
miners that passed this check; your own earlier models (same hotkey or coldkey) are never held
against you.

A submission is rejected as a duplicate, and its hotkey is spent, only when it is the same
model as such a one: identical tensors, an error correlating with that model's at `COPY_CORR`
(0.9999) or more over the whole model, or tensors holding `COPIED_FRAC` (99%) of its error each
correlating at `PART_CORR` (0.9999) or more (`src/model_dedup/config.py`). A model you trained
on from a king is yours: its error is still mostly the king's (a fine-tune moves it by a few
percent, a correlation of about 0.999) and it passes; the eval then holds it to the same bar as
any model, the margin over the current king. The same deterministic recipe run on the same data
gives the same model: if someone submitted it first, yours is the duplicate. Re-uploading a king
with a little noise does not pay: it passes this check and loses its duel.

## How a submission is judged

The evaluation dataset is the Hugging Face Parquet dataset and split named in `chain.toml`
`[dataset]`. The evaluator draws `SAMPLES_PER_DOMAIN` prompts from every domain, seeded by the
block hash of your `r2ready` commitment. Inside a domain it spreads the draw as evenly as possible
over the languages available there, then picks rows at random from each language; the seed makes
the same draw reproducible on every validator (`eval_service/dataset.py`). The teacher answers each prompt
(temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, at most `MAX_TOKENS` tokens); the king and your model
then read exactly the teacher's prompt and answer, in vLLM. Only the answer tokens are scored.
For each model, per answer token:

- KL: KL(teacher ‖ model) between the next-token distributions.
- Distance: |h_model − h_teacher| / |h_teacher|, the hidden state's distance from the teacher's
  as a fraction of the teacher's length, averaged over the layers in `LAYERS`.

Lower is better. The teacher rereading its own answer gives the noise floor, recorded with
every eval: batching alone makes two runs of the same model differ by about that much.

You win if your KL is lower than the king's by at least `KL_MARGIN` (1.5%) of the king's KL, and
your distance lower than the king's by at least `DIST_MARGIN` (0.84%) of the king's distance, both
measured in the same eval: both, so a large gain on one cannot make up for a loss on the other.
The margins are shares of the king's score, so the absolute bar shrinks as kings near the teacher.
The margins, the sample count and the layers are in `src/eval_service/config.py`. A win makes
you the new king immediately; a loss is final for that hotkey.

## Who gets paid

`src/common/reign.py`: the newest `SLOTS` (5) kings each receive
`SHARE` (0.2) of the emission for `REIGN_DAYS` (5) after their coronation. A king stops
earning when its reign is over or when five newer kings exist, whichever comes first. Whatever
is not assigned goes to uid 0. One king: 20% to it, 80% burned. Five fresh kings: 20% each.

A king whose uid is re-registered by another hotkey loses its share.

## Hotkeys

- One submission per hotkey. Once a model is evaluated, win or lose, the hotkey is spent.
- A submission that fails validation hands the upload attempt back; up to
  `MAX_UPLOAD_ATTEMPTS` (3) per hotkey (`src/chain_reader/config.py`).
- A submission rejected as a duplicate spends the hotkey; no attempt is handed back.
- A hotkey swap (same uid, same registration block, new hotkey) bars the new hotkey.
- Identical model bytes cannot be submitted twice, by anyone.

## Submitting a model

Your model never goes to a public URL. It is uploaded to the subnet's private bucket and only
becomes public if it wins.

1. `r2activate:v2:<family>:<quant>:<base64url pubkey>` — you declare the model family and
   quantization you upload (a pair listed in `chain.toml` `[upload_limits]`,
   today only `qwen38_27b:fp8`); the CLI takes `--family` / `--quant`, defaulting to genesis. It
   generates a one-time Ed25519 key and commits its public half on chain. An unlisted pair gets
   no credentials. Your upload limit and the validation rules are those of the declared pair. The validator mints storage credentials scoped to your own
   folder, encrypts them to that key and publishes them in a public mailbox.
2. The CLI decrypts the credentials and uploads the model files.
3. `r2ready:v2:<model digest>` — freezes the upload. The digest is one sha256 over every file's
   path, size and sha256. The validator revokes the credentials, checks the file names and the
   upload limit, re-hashes every byte against the digest when it downloads the model, and
   queues the submission for validation and evaluation.

Budgets: `UPLOAD_WINDOW_S` (24 h) from activate to ready; an upload is at most the
`[upload_limits]` entry for the pair you declared (35 GB for `qwen38_27b.fp8`); going over
it closes the upload and deletes it; bytes are kept `RETENTION_HOURS` (72) after they are no longer needed. Your status, including attempts
left and the reason for any rejection, is published as plaintext at
`<mailbox_url>/mailbox/v1/<registration_id>/status.json`; the CLI reads it for you.

Local state lives in `./.ingot-miner/<hotkey>/`: `submission-key` must survive from
activate to ready on the same machine; `upload-auth.json` is removed at ready.

## The CLI

```
uv sync && cp .env.example_miners .env         # INGOT_COLDKEY, INGOT_HOTKEY, netuid, network
uv run ingot register                          # burned registration
uv run ingot check-model --path ./my-model
uv run ingot submit-private --path ./my-model    # activate → upload → ready
uv run ingot activate                          # the same, one step at a time
uv run ingot upload-private --path ./my-model
uv run ingot ready --model-digest <hash>
```

Every flag defaults to the matching `INGOT_*` value in `.env`. `--yes` skips the confirm
prompts. The mailbox URL and the chain generation come from `chain.toml`; nothing else needs
configuring.
